effect: Major powers accepted the policy on paper, protecting U.S. commercial access to East Asia.
causes: American fear of being locked out of Chinese markets by European spheres of influence
effects: Acceptance by major powers on paper
Protection of U.S. commercial access to East Asia
significance: Shifted American foreign policy toward aggressive economic expansion in the Pacific arena

title: Theodore Roosevelt's Square Deal
description: Roosevelt pressed coal operators and striking miners into arbitration and sued the Northern Securities railroad combination, casting the presidency as a neutral referee between capital and labor.
cause: A five-month anthracite strike threatened winter fuel shortages while public anger at railroad and industrial trusts demanded action from Washington.
effect: Both sides accepted arbitration in October, and Roosevelt described the settlement as a square deal for labor and management alike.
causes: Anthracite miners struck in May 1902 over wages, hours, and union recognition
Coal shortages threatened Eastern cities as winter approached
Progressive pressure to check the power of consolidated corporations
effects: Roosevelt threatened federal seizure of the mines to force arbitration
The commission's 1903 award gave miners a 10 percent raise and a nine-hour day
The Justice Department sued Northern Securities under the Sherman Act
significance: First presidential intervention in a strike that did not simply break the union
Established the federal government as an active regulator of big business

title: Meat Inspection Act & Pure Food and Drug Act
description: Federal laws regulated consumer health standards and food production facilities.
cause: Publication of Upton Sinclair's muckraking novel The Jungle, exposing graphic unsanitary conditions in meatpacking plants.
effect: Created consumer protection agencies, mandatory ingredient labeling, and inspection of meatpacking plants.
causes: Publication of Upton Sinclair's muckraking novel The Jungle
Exposing graphic unsanitary conditions in meatpacking plants
effects: Creation of consumer protection agencies
Truthful labeling, including disclosure of specified dangerous or habit-forming ingredients
Ban on adulterated or misbranded food and drugs
Inspection of meatpacking plants
significance: Expanded federal regulatory power over corporate commerce
Prioritized public welfare over unregulated corporate profits

title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
description: An industrial disaster in New York City killed 146 young immigrant garment workers.
cause: Locked exit doors to prevent theft, lack of fire escapes, and poor safety oversight by factory bosses.
effect: Public outrage led to passage of some of the nation's strictest factory safety codes and labor laws in New York.
causes: Locked exit doors to prevent theft
Lack of fire escapes
Poor safety oversight by factory bosses
effects: Public outrage
Passage of some of the nation's strictest factory safety codes and labor laws in New York
significance: Galvanized the labor reform movement
Forced the state to take direct legal responsibility for workplace safety

title: Federal Reserve Act & 16th/17th Amendments
description: A central national bank was created while the income tax and direct election of senators were ratified.
cause: The financial panic of 1907 and Progressive demands to weaken corporate trusts and democratize political systems.
effect: Stabilized the national currency, shifted tax burdens to high earners, and diminished the power of state political bosses.
causes: Financial panic of 1907
Progressive demands to weaken corporate trusts and democratize political systems
effects: Stabilized the national currency
Shifted tax burdens to high earners
Diminished power of state political bosses
significance: Restructured the American economic and political framework
Created the modern regulatory state apparatus

title: The Great Migration
description: Black southerners left the rural South for northern and midwestern cities in rising numbers after 1916, part of a movement that continued for decades.
cause: Wartime factory work opened northern jobs just as European immigration collapsed, while Jim Crow and sharecropping debt pushed families out of the South.
effect: Roughly half a million Black southerners moved north between 1916 and 1919, transforming cities such as Chicago, Detroit, and New York.
causes: Wartime halt to European immigration created northern labor shortages
Northern factory wages far exceeded southern farm pay
Jim Crow segregation, lynching, and sharecropping debt
effects: Rapid growth of Black communities in northern cities
Labor recruiters offered free rail passage north
Competition over housing and jobs sparked white violence
significance: Shifted Black political and cultural life into northern cities
Built the urban base for the later civil rights movement

title: Espionage and Sedition Acts & Schenck v. United States
description: Laws criminalized anti-war speech; the Supreme Court ruled speech posing a 'clear and present danger' could be restricted.
cause: Wartime need for national unity and anti-draft protests led by socialists like Charles Schenck.
effect: Imprisoned anti-war dissidents like Eugene Debs and suppressed radical labor unions.
causes: Wartime need for national unity
Fear of socialist, IWW, and anti-draft agitation
Hysteria over suspected German sympathizers
effects: Imprisonment of anti-war dissidents (e.g., Eugene Debs)
Suppression of radical labor unions
significance: Demonstrated that civil liberties are often drastically curtailed by the federal government during national crises

title: U.S. Enters World War I
description: President Woodrow Wilson asked Congress for a declaration of war against Germany.
cause: Unrestricted German submarine warfare, interception of the Zimmermann Telegram, and desire to make the world safe for democracy.
effect: Deployment of American Expeditionary Forces tipped the military balance to the Allies and created a wartime command economy.
causes: Unrestricted German submarine warfare
Interception of the Zimmermann Telegram
Desire to make the world 'safe for democracy'
effects: Deployment of the American Expeditionary Forces
Tipping of the military balance to the Allies
Creation of a wartime command economy
significance: Marked the first large-scale U.S. military intervention in a European war, though non-interventionism revived until 1941

title: First Red Scare & Palmer Raids
description: Attorney General Palmer deported hundreds of suspected radicals without trial.
cause: The Bolshevik Revolution in Russia, a wave of postwar domestic labor strikes, and anarchist package bombings.
effect: Climate of fear, suppression of civil liberties, and rise of intense institutional nativism.
causes: Bolshevik Revolution in Russia
Wave of postwar domestic labor strikes
Anarchist package bombings
effects: Climate of fear
Suppression of civil liberties
Rise of intense institutional nativism
significance: Ignited a wave of xenophobia that reshaped immigration policy
Restricted political dissent for a decade

title: Treaty of Versailles & Rejection of the League of Nations
description: The treaty ending World War I was signed in June 1919, but the Senate refused to ratify it and kept the United States out of the League of Nations.
cause: Wilson's insistence on an unaltered treaty collided with Senate Republicans who feared its collective security clause would commit American troops without congressional consent.
effect: The Senate defeated both the unamended treaty and Henry Cabot Lodge's reserved version in November 1919, leaving the United States outside the League.
causes: Wilson's refusal to accept Lodge's reservations
Republican control of the Senate after the 1918 elections
Fear that Article X eroded congressional war powers
effects: Senate votes failed in November 1919 and again in March 1920
The United States never joined the League of Nations
A separate peace with Germany was concluded in 1921
significance: Signaled a retreat toward interwar isolationism
Weakened the League's capacity to deter later aggression

title: 19th Amendment Ratified
description: Women gained the constitutional right to vote in all U.S. elections.
cause: Decades of suffragist organizing, women's wartime service in WWI, and President Wilson's belated support.
effect: Enfranchised millions of women, though literacy tests and poll taxes continued to block many women of color.
causes: 72 years of suffragist organizing since Seneca Falls (1848)
Women's massive contributions to the World War I effort strengthened the case for suffrage
effects: Enfranchised approximately 26 million women
Literacy tests and poll taxes still prevented most Southern Black women from voting
significance: Largest single expansion of voting rights in American history
Demonstrated that sustained organized activism could achieve constitutional change

title: National Origins Act
description: Immigration law established a strict 2% quota based on the 1890 census to restrict immigration.
cause: Nativism fueled by the Red Scare and desire to block immigration from Southern and Eastern Europe.
effect: Drastically reduced immigration and near-totally excluded Asian immigrants.
causes: Nativism fueled by the Red Scare
Desire to block immigration from Southern and Eastern Europe
effects: Drastic reduction in immigration
Near-total exclusion of Asian immigrants
significance: Made permanent and far harsher the quota system created by the Emergency Quota Act of 1921, shifting the base to the 1890 census to curtail Southern and Eastern European immigration
Created a closed legal system

title: Scopes Trial & 1920s Cultural Conflict
description: Tennessee teacher John Scopes was tried in July 1925 for teaching evolution, in a nationally publicized courtroom clash over science, religion, and modern life.
cause: Tennessee's Butler Act banned teaching human evolution in public schools, and the ACLU offered to fund a test case that Dayton boosters recruited John Scopes to bring.
effect: Scopes was convicted and fined $100, though Clarence Darrow's cross-examination of William Jennings Bryan embarrassed fundamentalists in the national press.
causes: Tennessee's Butler Act barring evolution instruction
ACLU search for a test case to challenge the law
Fundamentalist backlash against modern urban culture
effects: Guilty verdict and a $100 fine for Scopes
Darrow's questioning of Bryan drew nationwide ridicule
Conviction later reversed on a legal technicality
significance: Dramatized the 1920s split between rural traditionalism and urban modernism
Framed a science-and-religion school debate that persists today

title: Stock Market Crash (Black Tuesday)
description: A sudden, catastrophic collapse of prices on the New York Stock Exchange triggered the Great Depression.
cause: Stock speculation, buying on margin, overproduction in agriculture and industry, and systemic banking instability.
effect: Global bank failures, skyrocketing unemployment reaching 25%, and collapse of consumer spending.
causes: Stock speculation
Buying on margin
Overproduction in agriculture/industry
Systemic banking instability
effects: Global bank failures
Skyrocketing unemployment (25%)
Collapse of consumer spending
significance: Triggered the Great Depression
Destroyed faith in unbridled laissez-faire capitalism

title: New Deal Begins
description: FDR launched sweeping federal programs to provide relief, recovery, and reform during the Great Depression.
cause: The Great Depression left a quarter of Americans unemployed and previous administrations' laissez-faire policies had failed.
effect: Permanently expanded the federal government's role in the economy and created the modern social safety net.
causes: 25% unemployment and massive bank failures demanded unprecedented government intervention
Hoover's laissez-faire approach failed to stop the economic collapse
effects: Created Social Security, the FDIC, the SEC, and other lasting federal institutions
Established the Democratic coalition of labor, minorities, and liberals that dominated politics for decades
significance: Fundamentally redefined the relationship between the federal government and American citizens
Created the modern regulatory state and social safety net that still exists today

title: Social Security Act & the Second New Deal
description: Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act in August 1935, pairing old-age pensions and unemployment insurance with the WPA's jobs program in a bolder phase of the New Deal.
cause: Stubborn unemployment, popular pressure from Huey Long and Francis Townsend, and the Supreme Court's rejection of early programs pushed Roosevelt toward broader reform.
effect: The act created payroll-funded pensions, unemployment insurance, and aid to dependent children, while the Wagner Act secured union organizing rights.
causes: Persistent mass unemployment after the First New Deal
Popular pressure from Townsend clubs and Huey Long
Supreme Court invalidation of the National Recovery Administration
effects: Payroll-funded old-age pensions and unemployment insurance
Wagner Act guaranteed private-sector collective bargaining
Farm and domestic workers excluded from initial coverage
significance: Laid the foundation of the American welfare state
Cemented the New Deal coalition that dominated politics for decades

title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
description: Japan's surprise attack on the U.S. naval base brought America into World War II.
cause: Japan sought to neutralize American naval power while it expanded its empire in Asia and the Pacific.
effect: United American public opinion behind the war effort and brought the U.S. into WWII the following day.
causes: U.S. oil embargo threatened Japan's imperial expansion in Asia
Japan calculated that a preemptive strike would cripple U.S. naval response
effects: Ended American isolationism and unified public opinion for war
Led to the forced internment of Japanese Americans under Executive Order 9066
significance: Ended U.S. isolationism and transformed America into the world's dominant military power
The internment of Japanese Americans remains one of the most significant civil liberties violations in U.S. history

title: Executive Order 9066 / Japanese Internment
description: 120,000 Japanese-Americans were forcibly relocated to inland concentration camps.
cause: Anti-Japanese racism, wartime paranoia following Pearl Harbor, and false fears of domestic sabotage.
effect: Loss of homes, businesses, and property while the Supreme Court upheld the order in Korematsu v. U.S.
causes: Anti-Japanese racism
Wartime paranoia following Pearl Harbor
False fears of domestic sabotage
effects: Loss of homes, businesses, and property
Supreme Court upholds the order in Korematsu v. U.S.
significance: One of the most egregious violations of constitutional civil liberties in American history
Driven by wartime panic and racial prejudice

title: D-Day and the Liberation of Western Europe
description: Allied forces landed on five Normandy beaches on June 6, 1944, opening the long-delayed western front against Nazi Germany.
cause: Stalin had pressed his allies for years to open a second front in the west and relieve Soviet armies fighting Germany in the east.
effect: Roughly 156,000 troops came ashore on the first day, and Allied armies broke out of Normandy to liberate Paris in late August.
causes: Soviet demands for a second front against Germany
Years of Allied buildup of troops and landing craft in Britain
Deception operations that misled Germany about the landing site
effects: About 156,000 Allied troops landed on the first day
Paris liberated in late August 1944
Germany trapped in a two-front war it could not sustain
significance: Launched the campaign that ended the European war in May 1945
Positioned Anglo-American armies to shape postwar Western Europe

title: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
description: The U.S. dropped two atomic weapons on Japanese cities, forcing unconditional surrender.
cause: The Manhattan Project and the desire to avoid a costly amphibious invasion of mainland Japan.
effect: Hundreds of thousands of civilian casualties and the immediate end of World War II.
causes: The Manhattan Project
Desire to avoid a costly amphibious invasion of mainland Japan
Desire to demonstrate power to the USSR
effects: Hundreds of thousands of civilian casualties
Immediate end of World War II
significance: Ushered humanity into the nuclear age
Acted as the opening geopolitical volley of the Cold War

title: Truman Doctrine & Marshall Plan
description: The U.S. pledged military aid to anti-communist nations and gave $13 billion to rebuild war-torn Western Europe.
cause: Soviet expansionism in Eastern Europe and fears that poverty would make Western Europe vulnerable to communism.
effect: Successful economic recovery of Western Europe and containment of communism in Greece and Turkey.
causes: Soviet expansionism in Eastern Europe
Fears that poverty would make Western Europe vulnerable to communism
effects: Successful economic recovery of Western Europe
Containment of communism in Greece and Turkey
significance: Established containment as the foundation of American foreign policy for the entire Cold War era

title: NATO Founded & the Berlin Airlift
description: The United States and eleven allies signed the North Atlantic Treaty in April 1949, while Allied planes supplied West Berlin through a Soviet blockade lifted that May, flying on until September.
cause: The Soviet blockade of West Berlin, begun in June 1948, convinced Western governments that containment required a standing peacetime military alliance.
effect: Twelve nations pledged mutual defense under Article 5, and Stalin lifted the Berlin blockade on May 12, 1949.
causes: Soviet blockade of West Berlin beginning in June 1948
Western fear of Soviet pressure on a divided Germany
Doubts that economic aid alone could contain communism
effects: Article 5 bound members to collective defense
Stalin lifted the Berlin blockade in May 1949
Soviets answered with the Warsaw Pact in 1955
significance: Broke the American tradition of avoiding peacetime alliances
Locked Europe into rival military blocs for the rest of the Cold War

title: Korean War
description: A Cold War proxy conflict ended in a stalemate at the 38th parallel.
cause: Communist North Korea invaded capitalist South Korea and the U.S. applied the containment doctrine via the UN.
effect: Mass casualties, massive expansion of the U.S. military budget, and integration of the military.
causes: Communist North Korea invades capitalist South Korea
U.S. applies containment doctrine via the UN
effects: Mass casualties
Massive expansion of the U.S. military budget (NSC-68 implemented)
Integration of the military
significance: The first hot military clash of the Cold War
Demonstrated U.S. willingness to fight to halt communist expansion

title: McCarthyism & the Second Red Scare
description: Senator Joseph McCarthy claimed in February 1950 to hold a list of communists working inside the State Department, fueling years of loyalty investigations and blacklisting.
cause: The Soviet atomic test, the communist victory in China, and high-profile espionage cases convinced many Americans that subversives had infiltrated the federal government.
effect: Government employees, teachers, and entertainers faced loyalty hearings, and Congress passed the McCarran Internal Security Act over Truman's veto.
causes: Soviet atomic bomb test in 1949
Communist victory in China's civil war
Alger Hiss perjury conviction and atomic espionage arrests
effects: Loyalty hearings and an entertainment industry blacklist
McCarran Internal Security Act passed over Truman's veto
Careers destroyed on thin or fabricated evidence
significance: Showed how fear of subversion can override civil liberties
McCarthy's 1954 Senate censure marked the limits of demagoguery

title: Brown v. Board of Education
description: The Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional.
cause: NAACP lawyers, led by Thurgood Marshall, challenged separate-but-equal schooling as inherently unequal.
effect: Overturned Plessy v. Ferguson and accelerated the Civil Rights Movement by legitimizing integration.
causes: NAACP pursued a deliberate legal strategy to dismantle Jim Crow through the courts
Psychologist Kenneth Clark's doll experiments showed the psychological harm of segregation
effects: Overturned Plessy v. Ferguson's 'separate but equal' doctrine
Galvanized the Civil Rights Movement and triggered massive resistance in the South
significance: Most consequential Supreme Court decision of the 20th century
Demonstrated that the 14th Amendment could be used as a tool for racial equality

title: Montgomery Bus Boycott
description: A year-long economic protest by Black citizens resulted in the desegregation of city buses.
cause: The arrest of Rosa Parks for refusing to yield her seat to a white passenger and organizing work by local activists.
effect: The Supreme Court ruled bus segregation unconstitutional and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. emerged as a national leader.
causes: Arrest of Rosa Parks for refusing to yield her seat to a white passenger
Organizing work by local activists
effects: Supreme Court rules bus segregation unconstitutional
Emergence of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. as a national leader
significance: Demonstrated the immense power of nonviolent mass direct action to overturn entrenched segregation laws

title: Little Rock Nine / Sputnik Launched
description: Federal troops protected Black students integrating a high school while the USSR launched the first artificial satellite.
cause: The Arkansas Governor used the National Guard to block school integration while the Soviets advanced in space technology.
effect: Eisenhower federalized the National Guard to enforce integration while creating NASA with funding for science education.
causes: Arkansas Governor uses the National Guard to block school integration
Soviet strides in space technology
effects: Eisenhower federalizes the National Guard to enforce integration
Creation of NASA
Funding for science education
significance: Showcased federal supremacy over states' rights
Intensified the global Cold War space and education race

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
description: A tense 13-day nuclear standoff between the U.S. and the Soviet Union over missiles in Cuba.
cause: Soviet deployment of nuclear missiles to Cuba following the failed U.S. Bay of Pigs invasion.
effect: Soviets removed missiles from Cuba while the U.S. removed missiles from Turkey; a direct hotline was installed.
causes: Soviet deployment of nuclear missiles to Cuba following the failed U.S. Bay of Pigs invasion
effects: Soviets remove missiles
U.S. removes missiles from Turkey
Installation of a direct Washington-Moscow hotline
significance: The closest the world ever came to a total, catastrophic thermonuclear war

title: March on Washington
description: About 250,000 demonstrators gathered at the Lincoln Memorial on August 28, 1963, demanding civil rights legislation and economic opportunity for Black Americans.
cause: Labor and civil rights leaders organized a mass rally to force Kennedy's stalled civil rights bill onto the national agenda.
effect: Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' address reached a live television audience and built pressure behind the bill that became the Civil Rights Act.
causes: Kennedy's civil rights bill stalled in Congress
Persistent job discrimination and unequal wages
Organizing by A. Philip Randolph, Bayard Rustin, and allied unions
effects: King delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech
Nationwide television coverage widened public sympathy
Momentum built toward the Civil Rights Act of 1964
significance: Became the defining image of nonviolent mass protest in America
Tied demands for legal equality to economic justice

title: Civil Rights Act of 1964
description: Landmark legislation outlawed discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
cause: Televised brutality against peaceful protesters and the assassination of JFK created political will for reform.
effect: Prohibited employment discrimination and segregation in public places, transforming American society.
causes: Televised footage of Bull Connor's fire hoses and police dogs in Birmingham shocked the nation
LBJ used JFK's assassination to push for the stalled civil rights bill
effects: Outlawed segregation in public accommodations and employment discrimination
Created the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC)
significance: Most comprehensive civil rights legislation since Reconstruction
Extended protections to women and other minorities beyond race

title: Gulf of Tonkin Resolution
description: Congress authorized the President to take all necessary measures in Vietnam after alleged attacks on U.S. destroyers.
cause: Alleged attacks on U.S. destroyers by North Vietnamese torpedo boats in the Gulf of Tonkin.
effect: Massive escalation and Americanization of the Vietnam War with deployment of over 500,000 ground troops.
causes: Alleged attacks on U.S. destroyers by North Vietnamese torpedo boats in the Gulf of Tonkin
effects: Massive escalation and Americanization of the Vietnam War
Deployment of over 500,000 ground troops
significance: Granted the executive branch a blank check to wage war without a formal congressional declaration

title: The Great Society
description: Johnson drove a sweeping reform program through Congress in 1965, creating Medicare and Medicaid and sending the first large federal aid to public schools.
cause: Johnson's landslide 1964 victory gave Democrats lopsided congressional majorities and a mandate to extend the New Deal into health care, education, and poverty relief.
effect: Medicare and Medicaid began covering the elderly and the poor, while federal grants flowed to schools in low-income districts.
causes: Democratic landslide in the 1964 elections
Johnson's declared War on Poverty
New attention to poverty amid general prosperity
effects: Medicare and Medicaid signed into law in July 1965
Elementary and Secondary Education Act funded poorer school districts
Head Start, Job Corps, and other antipoverty programs expanded
significance: Largest expansion of federal social programs since the New Deal
Provoked a conservative backlash against federal spending and regulation

title: Voting Rights Act & Immigration Act of 1965
description: Laws banned literacy tests and placed voting under federal oversight while abolishing the 1924 national origins quotas.
cause: Selma-to-Montgomery marches, civil rights pressures, and desire to remove discriminatory immigration structures.
effect: Dramatic increase in Black voter registration and a massive demographic shift as Asian and Latin American immigration surged.
causes: Selma-to-Montgomery marches
Civil rights pressures
Desire to remove discriminatory immigration structures
effects: Dramatic increase in Black voter registration
Massive demographic shift as Asian and Latin American immigration surges
significance: Permanently transformed the electorate
Democratized both the polling booth and the nation's demographic makeup

title: Tet Offensive
description: A massive coordinated surprise assault by North Vietnamese and Vietcong forces across South Vietnam shattered public support for the war.
cause: Vietcong desire to shatter South Vietnamese stability and break U.S. political resolve.
effect: Military defeat for the Vietcong but a massive psychological victory that widened the domestic 'credibility gap'.
causes: Hanoi's aim to shatter South Vietnamese stability and spark a general uprising
Intent to break U.S. political resolve
effects: Military defeat for the Vietcong
Massive psychological victory
Widening of the domestic 'credibility gap'
significance: The definitive political turning point of the Vietnam War
Turned the majority of the American public against the conflict

title: Earth Day & the Creation of the EPA
description: Some 20 million Americans joined the first Earth Day in April 1970, and the Environmental Protection Agency began operating that December.
cause: Visible pollution disasters, including the 1969 Santa Barbara oil spill and the burning Cuyahoga River, pushed environmental concern into mainstream politics.
effect: Nixon and Congress consolidated federal pollution enforcement in the new EPA and strengthened the Clean Air Act before the year ended.
causes: 1969 Santa Barbara oil spill and Cuyahoga River fire
Rachel Carson's Silent Spring and a growing ecology movement
Senator Gaylord Nelson's call for a national environmental teach-in
effects: About 20 million Americans took part in the first Earth Day
EPA created in December 1970 to enforce pollution law
Clean Air Act amendments set national air quality standards
significance: Made environmental protection a permanent federal responsibility
Opened lasting conflicts between regulation and industry costs

title: Nixon's Visit to China & Détente
description: Nixon spent a week in China in February 1972, ending more than two decades of American nonrecognition and opening a period of eased Cold War tensions.
cause: Nixon and Kissinger sought to exploit the Sino-Soviet split for leverage over Moscow and help in extracting the United States from Vietnam.
effect: The Shanghai Communiqué set terms for future relations, and three months later Nixon signed the SALT I arms agreements in Moscow.
causes: Deep hostility between China and the Soviet Union
Nixon's search for leverage to end the Vietnam War
Secret groundwork laid by Henry Kissinger in 1971
effects: Shanghai Communiqué issued on February 28, 1972
SALT I and the ABM Treaty signed in Moscow that May
Path opened to full U.S.-China diplomatic relations in 1979
significance: Replaced rigid containment with triangular great-power diplomacy
Reordered Cold War alignments for the following two decades

title: OPEC Oil Embargo & Stagflation
description: Arab oil producers cut shipments to the United States in October 1973 over its support for Israel, driving fuel prices up and deepening a decade of stagflation.
cause: Arab members of OPEC retaliated for American military resupply of Israel during the Yom Kippur War.
effect: Crude prices roughly quadrupled within months, gasoline lines formed nationwide, and inflation climbed alongside rising unemployment.
causes: U.S. military aid to Israel during the Yom Kippur War
OPEC's growing control over world oil pricing
Heavy American dependence on imported petroleum
effects: Crude oil prices roughly quadrupled by early 1974
Long gasoline lines and a national 55 mph speed limit
Inflation and unemployment rose together as stagflation
significance: Ended the postwar era of cheap and abundant energy
Made energy policy a permanent concern of American politics

title: Paris Peace Accords
description: A treaty ended direct United States military involvement in the Vietnam War.
cause: Unending domestic anti-war protests, high military casualties, and Nixon's 'Peace with Honor' strategy.
effect: Withdrawal of all U.S. combat troops and return of American POWs, leading to the eventual fall of Saigon in 1975.
causes: Unending domestic anti-war protests
High military casualties
Nixon's 'Peace with Honor' strategy
effects: Withdrawal of all U.S. combat troops
Return of American POWs
Eventual fall of Saigon to North Vietnam in 1975
significance: Concluded the longest and most divisive foreign war in American history up to that point
Left deep cultural scars

title: Roe v. Wade
description: The Supreme Court ruled that the constitutional right to privacy protected a woman's right to choose an abortion.
cause: The rise of the Second Wave Feminist Movement and legal challenges to restrictive state abortion laws.
effect: State abortion bans were struck down and abortion emerged as a polarizing political issue.
causes: The rise of the Second Wave Feminist Movement
Legal challenges to restrictive state abortion laws
effects: Striking down of state abortion bans
Emergence of abortion as a polarizing political issue
significance: Redefined constitutional privacy protections
Acted as a major catalyst for the rise of the Religious Right

title: Watergate Scandal & Resignation of Nixon
description: Richard Nixon became the first U.S. president to resign from office amid the Watergate scandal.
cause: A break-in at Democratic National Committee headquarters and Nixon's extensive cover-up of the crime.
effect: Passage of campaign finance reforms and a deeply cynical public attitude toward federal politicians.
causes: Break-in at the Democratic National Committee headquarters
Nixon's extensive orchestrations to cover up the crime
effects: Passage of campaign finance reforms
Deeply cynical public attitude toward federal politicians
significance: Demonstrated that the constitutional system of checks and balances could successfully hold the executive branch accountable

title: Iranian Hostage Crisis
description: Iranian radicals seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran, holding 52 Americans hostage for 444 days.
cause: The Islamic Revolution in Iran and the U.S. admission of the deposed Shah into an American hospital for treatment.
effect: A failed rescue attempt and prolonged economic misery paralyzed the Carter presidency.
causes: Islamic Revolution in Iran
U.S. admits the deposed, cancer-stricken Shah into an American hospital for medical treatment
effects: Failed rescue attempt (Operation Eagle Claw)
Prolonged economic misery and inflation under the Carter administration
significance: Paralyzed the Carter presidency
Severely damaged public faith in American global dominance and strength

title: Election of Ronald Reagan
description: Conservative Republican Ronald Reagan defeated incumbent Democrat Jimmy Carter in a landslide.
cause: Stagflation, high unemployment, the Iranian Hostage Crisis, and growing public backlash against Great Society liberalism.
effect: Implementation of supply-side 'Reaganomics' including deregulation of industries and income tax cuts.
causes: Stagflation
High unemployment
Iranian Hostage Crisis
Growing public backlash against Great Society liberalism
effects: Implementation of supply-side economics ('Reaganomics')
Deregulation of industries
Cutting of income taxes
significance: Launched the Reagan Revolution

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: The peaceful destruction of the physical barrier separating East and West Berlin symbolized the collapse of Soviet communism.
cause: Soviet economic stagnation, Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms of glasnost and perestroika, and Reagan's diplomatic pressure.
effect: German reunification and rapid collapse of communist regimes across Eastern Europe.
causes: Soviet economic stagnation
Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms (glasnost and perestroika)
Reagan's diplomatic pressure
effects: Reunification of Germany
Rapid collapse of communist regimes across Eastern Europe
significance: Symbolized the collapse of Soviet communism
Marked the beginning of the end of the Cold War, which formally concluded with the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991

title: Collapse of the Soviet Union & the Persian Gulf War
description: A U.S.-led coalition drove Iraq out of Kuwait early in 1991, and by December the Soviet Union had dissolved into fifteen independent republics.
cause: Iraq's seizure of Kuwait in August 1990 triggered a coalition response, while a failed hardline coup in August 1991 shattered Soviet central authority.
effect: Kuwait was liberated by late February 1991, and Gorbachev resigned that December as the Soviet state ceased to exist.
causes: Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990
Failed hardline coup against Gorbachev in August 1991
Soviet economic decline and nationalist movements in the republics
effects: Coalition air campaign opened on January 17, 1991
Kuwait retaken after a ground war of roughly 100 hours
Gorbachev resigned and fifteen republics became independent states
significance: Left the United States as the world's sole superpower
Set the stage for sustained American military involvement in the Middle East

title: NAFTA & the Globalized Economy
description: NAFTA took effect on January 1, 1994, phasing out tariffs among the United States, Canada, and Mexico and creating one of the world's largest trading blocs.
cause: Bush negotiated and signed the agreement in 1992, and Clinton won congressional approval in 1993 by arguing that open markets would expand American exports.
effect: Trade and investment among the three countries grew rapidly, while manufacturers shifted production toward lower-wage plants in Mexico.
causes: Bush administration negotiations completed in 1992
Clinton's push for congressional approval in 1993
Belief that freer trade would boost exports and growth
effects: Tariffs phased out across North America
Cross-border trade and investment surged
Manufacturing jobs shifted toward lower-wage regions
significance: Made trade policy a lasting fault line in American politics
Deepened economic integration that later fueled populist backlash

title: September 11 Terrorist Attacks
description: Al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four commercial airplanes, destroying the World Trade Center towers and damaging the Pentagon.
cause: Radical Islamist opposition to U.S. military presence in the Middle East and support for Israel.
effect: Launched the global War on Terror with invasions of Afghanistan and Iraq, and passage of the USA PATRIOT Act.

Support for Israel
effects: Launch of the global War on Terror
Invasions of Afghanistan and Iraq
Passage of the controversial USA PATRIOT Act
significance: Fundamentally transformed American national security policy
Transformed domestic surveillance and foreign military entanglements

title: Election of Barack Obama & The Great Recession
description: The first African-American president was elected amidst the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.
cause: The subprime mortgage crisis, collapse of major Wall Street banks, and public exhaustion with the Iraq War.
effect: Passage of the Affordable Care Act and massive federal economic stimulus packages.

Collapse of major Wall Street banks
Public exhaustion with the protracted Iraq War
